newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to renew funding for Skase chase.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to renew funding for Skase chase.

text.p: Australian Attorney-General Daryl Williams said on Wednesday the government would have another look at pursuing failed media tycoon Christopher Skase, reversing an earlier decision to give up on the case.
"I have reviewed that decision, I invited (bankruptcy trustee) Mr Donnelly to make a fresh application, and have approved that application," Williams told reporters.

"The effect of which will be to provide further limited funding to enable Mr Donnelly to continue to investigate the prospect of recovering assets for the benefit of Mr Skase's creditors," said Williams, the country's chief legal officer.
Donnelly is the official appointed by the government to administer the bankruptcy.
The Australian government announced earlier in October it would review a decision to end funding for the attempted recovery of Skase's assets.
The government had previously said it would drop the case after assessing that further efforts to recover Skase's assets were unlikely to succeed.
The former Labor government spent A$14 million in a failed attempt to extradite Skase from Spain, where he now lives in self-imposed exile.
The failed tycoon declared himself bankrupt in 1991 with personal debts of A$80 million and left Australia for Spain.

Skase is still wanted in Australia on company charges relating to his failed business dealings, including 35 charges arising from the collapse of his A$1.5 billion Qintex media and entertainment empire.
